judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 5, which added sexual orientation and gender identity to the categories protected from discrimination in employment, housing, credit, education, jury service, and businesses open to the public. The House passed it 224-206.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 5, which added sexual orientation and gender identity to the categories protected from discrimination in employment, housing, credit, education, jury service, and businesses open to the public. The House passed it 224-206.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 803, the Protecting America's Wilderness and Public Lands Act, which designated new wilderness, conservation, and recreation areas on federal land across eight states and the Virgin Islands. The House passed it 227-200.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 803, the Protecting America's Wilderness and Public Lands Act, which designated new wilderness, conservation, and recreation areas on federal land across eight states and the Virgin Islands. The House passed it 227-200.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1280, which restricted chokeholds and no-knock warrants, made it easier to sue officers for misconduct, and created national standards and misconduct reporting for police. The House passed it 220-212.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1280, which restricted chokeholds and no-knock warrants, made it easier to sue officers for misconduct, and created national standards and misconduct reporting for police. The House passed it 220-212.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1319, the American Rescue Plan Act, the $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package that sent $1,400 payments to most households, extended jobless benefits, expanded the child tax credit, and funded vaccines, schools, and state governments. The Senate passed it 50-49.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1319, the American Rescue Plan Act, the $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package that sent $1,400 payments to most households, extended jobless benefits, expanded the child tax credit, and funded vaccines, schools, and state governments. The Senate passed it 50-49.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending H.R. 1319, to the President, agreeing to the Senate's version of the $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package that sent $1,400 payments to most households, extended jobless benefits, expanded the child tax credit, and funded vaccines and schools. The House passed it 220-211.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending H.R. 1319, the American Rescue Plan Act, to the President, which agreed to the Senate's version of the $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief package that sent $1,400 payments to most households, extended jobless benefits, expanded the child tax credit, and funded vaccines and schools. The House passed it 220-211.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act, which required a licensed dealer to run a background check on nearly every private firearm sale or transfer, including at gun shows and online. The House passed it 227-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act, which required a licensed dealer to run a background check on nearly every private firearm sale or transfer, including at gun shows and online. The House passed it 227-203.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1446, the Enhanced Background Checks Act, which extended the time a dealer must wait for a completed background check from three business days to at least ten, closing the so-called Charleston loophole. The House passed it 219-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1446, the Enhanced Background Checks Act, which extended the time a dealer must wait for a completed background check from three business days to at least ten, closing the so-called Charleston loophole. The House passed it 219-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 17, which removed the deadline for states to approve the Equal Rights Amendment, which would bar discrimination based on sex. The House passed it 222-204.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 17, which removed the deadline for states to approve the Equal Rights Amendment, which would bar discrimination based on sex. The House passed it 222-204.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1620, the Violence Against Women Act Reauthorization, which renewed federal programs against domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking through 2026 and added housing protections and firearm restrictions for convicted abusers. The House passed it 244-172.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1620, the Violence Against Women Act Reauthorization, which renewed federal programs against domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking through 2026 and added housing protections and firearm restrictions for convicted abusers. The House passed it 244-172.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 6, the American Dream and Promise Act, which offered green cards to immigrants brought to the country as children and people protected by temporary programs that prevent deportation. The House passed it 228-197.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 6, the American Dream and Promise Act, which offered green cards to immigrants brought to the country as children and people protected by temporary programs that prevent deportation. The House passed it 228-197.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1603, the Farm Workforce Modernization Act, which created legal status and a path to permanent residence for undocumented farmworkers, and reworked the H-2A program for seasonal farmworkers. The House passed it 247-174.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1603, the Farm Workforce Modernization Act, which created legal status and a path to permanent residence for undocumented farmworkers, and reworked the H-2A program for seasonal farmworkers. The House passed it 247-174.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1868, which paused automatic Medicare budget cuts through the end of 2021. The House passed it 246-175.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1868, which paused automatic Medicare budget cuts through the end of 2021. The House passed it 246-175.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 7, which narrowed the defenses an employer can raise for paying men and women differently, barred retaliation against workers who discuss pay, and strengthened workers' legal options in wage discrimination cases. The House passed it 217-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 7, which narrowed the defenses an employer can raise for paying men and women differently, barred retaliation against workers who discuss pay, and strengthened workers' legal options in wage discrimination cases. The House passed it 217-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1333, the NO BAN Act, which limited the President's power to bar entry to the United States and barred religious discrimination in visa and immigration decisions. The House passed it 218-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1333, the NO BAN Act, which limited the President's power to bar entry to the United States and barred religious discrimination in visa and immigration decisions. The House passed it 218-208.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1573, the Access to Counsel Act, which gave citizens, green card holders, visa holders, and returning refugees the right to consult a lawyer when held for extra screening at the border or an airport. The House passed it 217-207.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1573, the Access to Counsel Act, which gave citizens, green card holders, visa holders, and returning refugees the right to consult a lawyer when held for extra screening at the border or an airport. The House passed it 217-207.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 14 to cancel the 2020 EPA rule that had removed methane emission limits from new and modified oil and gas sources, restoring those standards. The Senate passed it 52-42.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 14 to cancel the 2020 EPA rule that had removed methane emission limits from new and modified oil and gas sources, restoring those standards. The Senate passed it 52-42.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1629, the Fairness in Orphan Drug Exclusivity Act, which limited seven years of sole-sales rights for rare-disease drugs to those not expected to make a profit. It failed 250-168 under a fast-track process needing two-thirds support, so it did not become law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1629, the Fairness in Orphan Drug Exclusivity Act, which limited seven years of sole-sales rights for rare-disease drugs to those not expected to make a profit. It failed 250-168 under a fast-track process needing two-thirds support, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 15 to cancel the federal bank regulator's true lender rule, a rule that let national banks be named as lender on loans funded by others and so shield them from state interest rate caps. The Senate passed it 52-47.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 15 to cancel the federal bank regulator's true lender rule, a rule that let national banks be named as lender on loans funded by others and so shield them from state interest rate caps. The Senate passed it 52-47.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 2547, the Comprehensive Debt Collection Improvement Act, which restricted debt collection practices, extended student loan protections to private loans, and limited collection on servicemembers and medical debt. The House passed it 215-207.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 2547, the Comprehensive Debt Collection Improvement Act, which restricted debt collection practices, extended student loan protections to private loans, and limited collection on servicemembers and medical debt. The House passed it 215-207.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1065, the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which required employers to make reasonable work changes for workers affected by pregnancy or childbirth. The House passed it 315-101.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1065, the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which required employers to make reasonable work changes for workers affected by pregnancy or childbirth. The House passed it 315-101.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1187, the Corporate Governance Improvement and Investor Protection Act, which required public companies to disclose climate risk, political spending, executive pay, and other environmental, social, and governance measures. The House passed it 215-214.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1187, the Corporate Governance Improvement and Investor Protection Act, which required public companies to disclose climate risk, political spending, executive pay, and other environmental, social, and governance measures. The House passed it 215-214.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 256, which repealed the 2002 law allowing military force against Iraq, withdrawing the standing legal basis for military action there. The House passed it 268-161.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 256, which repealed the 2002 law allowing military force against Iraq, withdrawing the standing legal basis for military action there. The House passed it 268-161.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 2062, the Protecting Older Workers Against Discrimination Act, which let workers win an age discrimination claim by showing age was a motivating factor rather than the sole cause. The House passed it 247-178.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 2062, the Protecting Older Workers Against Discrimination Act, which let workers win an age discrimination claim by showing age was a motivating factor rather than the sole cause. The House passed it 247-178.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending S.J.Res. 15 to the President to cancel the federal bank regulator's true lender rule, a rule that let national banks be named as lender on loans funded by others and so shield them from state interest rate caps. The House passed it 218-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 15 to the President to cancel the federal bank regulator's true lender rule, a rule that let national banks be named as lender on loans funded by others and so shield them from state interest rate caps. The House passed it 218-208.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1443, the LGBTQ Business Equal Credit Enforcement and Investment Act, which required lenders to report credit application data for LGBTQ-owned businesses so fair lending laws can be enforced. The House passed it 252-176.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1443, the LGBTQ Business Equal Credit Enforcement and Investment Act, which required lenders to report credit application data for LGBTQ-owned businesses so fair lending laws can be enforced. The House passed it 252-176.
